source.citation: "THE SAUGANASH HOTEL." — wood engraving, in A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, vol. 1 (Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1884), p. 632, in the chapter "Wolf Point and Early Hotels". A copyright line reading "A. T. Andreas, 188-" is lettered inside the plate border at the lower left.
what_it_does_not_supply: any coordinate, footprint outline or dimension
the hitching posts or the right-hand board fence the brief lists — not resolvable in this scan, and not claimed here
the engraver's name: no signature is legible, so the brief's Braunhold attribution stands unverified
a date for the scene, and a date for the plate only by way of the volume's 1884 imprint
what_it_supplies: the Sauganash's two-storey clapboard block with a chimney at each end of the ridge
the log wing running back at the left, lower, with its door direct to grade under a shed roof
a wide entrance surround at the centre of the front elevation
a plank walk along the front, returning round the corner of the block
the even two-storey rhythm of sash across the clapboard front
